title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-26
content:
Purpose:
Notes/scratchpad for dbg of throughput regression that started ~2025-02-09 after a config push to continuous-batching defaults. Rapid notes, commands tried, outputs, hypotheses, and next steps.

Summary / observed behavior:
- Cluster: hosted-prod-us-west (dedicated pool: dp-rt-4). Regression detected around 2025-02-09 03:14 UTC.
- Symptom: steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) fell ~30% p50->p95 latency increased ~20%, tail spikes. Token cost per second dropped but latency SLO violated.
- Related change: config push that adjusted continuous_batching.* defaults (PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra-config/commit/abc123) — max_batch_tokens from 1024 -> 512, batching_window_ms from 20 -> 10.
- KV cache hit rate dropped (see logs below).

Timeline (quick):
- 2025-02-09 02:50 UTC: config applied to staging (ok).
- 2025-02-09 03:10 UTC: config rolled to prod (canary then full).
- 2025-02-09 03:14 UTC: alert fired (throughput drop).
- 2025-02-09 03:20 UTC: first rollback attempt on frontend only (no effect).
- 2025-02-10 10:00 UTC: found KV cache miss rate up; started deep-dive.

Commands run / repro steps tried:
1) Quick smoke against hosted API (curl):
   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-67b", "input":"lorem ipsum"}' | jq .
   - result: responses OK but latency ~1.6x baseline.

2) Local load (wrk) to reproduce:
   wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --script=gen.lua https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
   - baseline (pre-change): ~120k tokens/s across canaries
   - post-change: ~85k tokens/s

3) Internal client test (python):
   python tests/load_repro.py --model rwd-67b --concurrency 32 --seq-len 512 --batching on
   - Observed worker logs show frequent small batches (size 1-2) vs expected 8-12.

4) k8s / host debugging:
   kubectl -n inference exec -it pod/serve-rt-7 -- bash
   ps aux | grep serve_runtime
   # tail logs
   grep "kv-cache" /var/log/serve/runtime.log | tail -n 40

   Sample log lines:
   2025-02-09T03:16:02Z INFO batching: batch formed size=2 tokens=80 window_ms=12
   2025-02-09T03:16:02Z WARN kv-cache: miss id=abc123 (miss rate=23.7%)
   2025-02-09T03:16:02Z INFO scheduler: enqueued request qlen=3

5) Metrics checked (datadog dashboards):
   - continuous_batching.batch_size.p50 dropped from 9 -> 3
   - continuous_batching.window_ms reported as 10 (matches new default)
   - kv_cache.hit_rate dropped from 97% -> 74% (correlates with more cache evictions)
   - scheduler.loop_time increased slightly, CPU steady, GPU utilization lower by ~12% (saturation not reached)

6) Reproduction on canary by flipping flags:
   # disable continuous batching on one canary host
   kubectl set env deploy/serve-rt CANARY_CONT_BATCHING=false -n inference
   -> immediate throughput on that host recovered to ~95% baseline; but global still low because other hosts still on config.

Commands that changed internal behavior (tested):
- toggle continuous_batching.enabled=false -> throughput restored locally
- increasing max_batch_tokens back to 1024 on a single worker -> larger batches formed, throughput improved
- toggling batching_window_ms from 10 to 25 -> slightly better batching, but tail latency increased in some cases

Error / log snippets copied:
- "batch formed size=1 tokens=12 window_ms=10 (forced flush)"
- "kv-cache: evicting key list length > threshold -> eviction_count=1421"
- "scheduler: request routed to fallback_unbatched_path (reason=token_overflow)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Shorter batching window + lower max_batch_tokens causes more frequent flushes with smaller batches, which increases per-token overhead and reduces throughput. (LIKELY)
2) New defaults interact badly with certain request length distributions — many requests are <50 tokens but frequent, so window too small to accumulate. (LIKELY)
3) KV-cache behavior: smaller batches cause different KV-cache lifecycle semantics (cold entries not being reused across micro-batches), increasing cache miss rate which forces extra compute. (PLAUSIBLE)
4) Router/scheduler regression: some requests being misclassified and routed to unbatched fallback path due to a token sizing edge-case introduced in config parsing. (POSSIBLE)
5) Memory pressure / GC: not evident (heap stable), so low probability.

Notes on KV-cache correlation:
- When batch size reduced, per-request KV-cache scope shortened (cache keys include batch-seq prefix) -> effective reuse reduces. Investigate whether KV cache keying uses request-id or full prefix. If key space increased, misses will rise.

What we've tried and the results:
- Rolling restart of frontends only -> no change.
- Flipping continuous_batching.enabled=false on a single worker -> host throughput recovers.
- Reverting entire config on a small canary group -> cluster recovery observed.
- Increase max_batch_tokens to 1024 on canary -> recovery but not identical to original baseline (window_ms still 10).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether config rollout wrote to all components (frontends + workers + router). I suspect router used old value while workers have new, or vice versa. ACTION: verify config hash on router pods.
- Check codepath where "fallback_unbatched_path" is chosen (search for token_overflow logic).
- Add a small unit/integration test that simulates short-window high-qps workload to catch this in staging.
- Add Datadog alert on continuous_batching.batch_size.p50 drop > 30% and kv_cache.hit_rate drop > 10% within 5m.
- Longer term: evaluate adaptive windowing (workload-aware) or request-type steering.

Immediate mitigation plan (recommended):
1) Roll back the config change cluster-wide to previous values (max_batch_tokens=1024, batching_window_ms=20) — stopgap until we fully understand.
2) Add rollback verification: run smoke scripts and metric checks for 10 min after roll.
3) Add canary gating: require min p50 throughput and kv_cache hit rate before full rollout.

Repro script references:
- tests/load_repro.py (repo: github.com/redwood/repro)
- gen.lua (wrk script)

Links / refs:
- PR with config change: https://github.com/redwood/infra-config/commit/abc123
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INC-5432
- Related docs: https://confluence.company/serving/continuous-batching-design

Notes to self (raw brainstorm):
- Could be that smaller window reduces opportunity for cross-request KV cache reuse. If KV cache keys are per-batch id, then smaller batches -> more unique keys -> misses. Need to check key scheme.
- Also verify kernel-level TCP Nagle interactions with smaller packets (unlikely given HTTP/2 and TCP_NODELAY on our stack but worth a thought).
- Consider a patch that ensures min_batch_delay_ms which ensures small requests get padded to wait N ms before flush if qlen below threshold.

Next steps (owners):
- Ava: revert config in infra-config and run canary verify (ASAP).
- Ravi: check router config and logs for fallback_unbatched_path classification (today).
- Lena: add datadog alerts and short-run integration test in repro repo (tomorrow).

If anything else I try I'll append here. This is a scratchpad; will convert to incident breadcrumbs for JIRA once we have final root cause.

-- Ava
